name: Jeong In-ji, An Ji and Gwon Je
credit: Page of the 1447 woodblock Yongbi eocheon ga (no portrait of the compilers exists) · Public domain (Wikimedia Commons). Text: Korean Wikisource.
bio: Jeong In-ji (鄭麟趾, 1396-1478), An Ji (安止, 1384-1464) and Gwon Je (權踶, 1387-1445) were scholar-officials of the Hall of Worthies at the court of King Sejong of Joseon. In 1445 the three presented to the throne the Yongbi eocheon ga (龍飛御天歌), "Songs of the Dragons Flying to Heaven", their commentary-annotated poem in praise of the dynasty.

The work has 125 cantos, each a short song in Middle Korean paired with a Classical Chinese rendering, with prose notes added to the printed edition of 1447. It celebrates the six "dragons", the ancestors and founders of the Joseon dynasty, and is one of the first works printed in the Korean alphabet, Hangul, promulgated in 1446. This archive gives the Middle Korean song text of each canto.
